claim: The countably infinite discrete case is introduced only by weights p_i≥0 with total sum 1.
analysis: Unlike the finite case, the text never declares the event sigma-algebra or defines the probability of a general event from these weights. Consequently it does not actually give the promised countable discrete probability construction, and a reader cannot directly verify the probability axioms from the displayed conditions.
evidence or derivation: For Omega={1,2,...}, the needed construction is A=2^Omega and P(A)=sum_{i in A}p_i. Nonnegative normalized weights make this sum well-defined; for pairwise disjoint events A_j, the index sets are disjoint, so regrouping the nonnegative double series gives P(union_j A_j)=sum_j P(A_j).
dependencies: Lines 132-148, including the heavy-tail and geometric examples, implicitly rely on this omitted mapping from point masses to event probabilities.
suggested_disposition: Add the event space and formula P(A)=sum_{i in A}p_i (with the appropriate index set) and one sentence noting countable additivity.

claim: The geometric-probability definition permits arbitrary Omega of merely finite volume and assigns P(A)=|A|/|Omega| to every subset A⊆Omega.
analysis: Lebesgue volume is not defined for every subset, so the formula cannot define a probability on all subsets. In addition, finite volume as written allows |Omega|=0, making the denominator zero. Measurability and 0<|Omega|<infinity are essential to a valid normalized-volume probability space.
evidence or derivation: Let Omega=[0,1]. A non-Lebesgue-measurable subset V⊆[0,1] has no Lebesgue volume |V|, so P(V) is undefined under the stated formula; replacing |·| by outer measure does not restore countable additivity. Separately, Omega={0} has finite volume 0, hence |A|/|Omega| is 0/0 for A=Omega. A valid version takes measurable Omega with 0<|Omega|<infinity and event sigma-algebra {A⊆Omega:A is Lebesgue measurable}.
dependencies: Lines 188-190 use the denominator and singleton calculation; lines 226-227 specialize conditional probability to this geometric construction.
suggested_disposition: State the positive finite Lebesgue-measure hypothesis, restrict events to measurable subsets of Omega, and define the corresponding sigma-algebra.

claim: Exercise 1 says to verify the additivity axiom but asks only the finite-union identity.
analysis: A3 at lines 14-15 is countable additivity. The requested finite result is correct and, on finite Omega, can be extended to A3 because a pairwise-disjoint countable family has at most N nonempty members; that reduction is not stated, so the exercise does not literally ask students to prove the named axiom.
evidence or derivation: If Omega has N points and A_j are pairwise disjoint, each nonempty A_j contains a distinct point, so at most N sets are nonempty. Countable additivity then reduces to the finite formula after deleting empty sets.
dependencies: Exercise 1's description refers back to A3 (lines 14-15) and the finite discrete construction (lines 106-115).
suggested_disposition: Either call the exercise 'finite additivity' or add the one-sentence argument reducing countable families to finite ones on a finite sample space.
